gloss: to catch; to capture; to seize

definitions.gloss: to catch; to capture; to seize (an animal, fish, criminal)
definitions.explanation: To physically catch or capture a moving creature or person — most often fish, insects, or game animals, or sometimes criminals. Used when the action involves chasing or grabbing.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}で{魚|さかな}を{捕|と}った。
examples.english: I caught fish in the river.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}は{何時間|なんじかん}もかけて{犯人|はんにん}を{捕|と}らえた。
examples.english: The police took several hours to apprehend the suspect.

notes:
Transitive godan verb ({五段|ごだん}, ら-row stem). One of several とる verbs distinguished mainly by kanji choice — {捕|と}る specifically means catching a moving target (animals, criminals).

TRANSITIVITY:
- Transitive: Xを{捕|と}る
- No common intransitive pair; {捕|と}まる (to be caught) is the related intransitive.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {魚|さかな}を{捕|と}る: to catch fish
- {虫|むし}を{捕|と}る: to catch insects
- {犯人|はんにん}を{捕|と}る: to catch a criminal
- {鼠|ねずみ}を{捕|と}る: to catch mice (often said of cats)

KANJI DISTINCTIONS (とる homophones):
- {取|と}る: to take, to pick up — most general, default choice
- {捕|と}る: to catch, to capture — moving prey or criminals (this entry)
- {採|と}る: to gather, to adopt — collecting samples, harvesting, hiring
- {撮|と}る: to take (a photo) — only for photos and video

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {捕|つか}まえる: to catch; to apprehend — emphasizes the act of grabbing hold; often interchangeable with {捕|と}る but more vivid
- {捕獲|ほかく}する: to capture (formal) — used for wildlife management, escapees, etc.
